clue.text: Type of cheese for university sportsperson?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a British blue cheese of that name
second meaning: someone who has represented Oxford University in a sport, earning a Blue

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one phrase: a cheese, and an Oxford athlete awarded a Blue, the colours given to those who compete for the university against Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a blue-veined cheese and an Oxford athlete who has won his or her colours.

clue.text: Choose not to participate in work followed by racecourse tipster

indicators.note: followed by puts the word for work first and the tipster after it

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a tout sells racing tips at the course

explanation.surface: Someone declines a job alongside a dodgy racing tipster.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to choose to withdraw from or not join in an arrangement.

clue.text: Conclusion of mostly excellent beer

indicators.note: mostly means the word for excellent loses its last letter

parts.note: fine means excellent
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: The end of an almost first-rate pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part or climax of a show or piece of music.

clue.text: Newly building up, stupidly cutting corners

indicators.note: stupidly suggests the words are handled foolishly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A builder is foolishly skimping on a rebuild.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconstructing is rebuilding, putting something up again after it was damaged or demolished.

clue.text: Reserves lofty stand for selling literary compositions

parts.note: to reserve a seat is to book it
lofty means tall

explanation.surface: Someone books a towering stand for selling novels.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookstall is a small stall or kiosk where books and magazines are sold.

clue.text: Female in small military group not in good condition

indicators.note: in means the female letter goes inside the word for the military group

parts.note: a unit is a military group

explanation.surface: A woman in a small army detachment is out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit means physically out of shape, lacking the required health or fitness.

clue.text: Mad zealot holds sharp object

indicators.note: the phrase Mad zealot holds the answer within its letters, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A fanatic is concealing a blade or other sharp weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a cutting tool with an arched blade set at right angles to the handle.

clue.text: Oddly dermic blood vessels — vehicle needed for these!

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of dermic, first, third and fifth

parts.note: veins are blood vessels

explanation.surface: Skin-deep veins, an odd medical aside that seems to demand an ambulance.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive-ins are cinemas or restaurants where customers stay in their cars, so you need a car to use them.

clue.text: Fraction of New York lights found here — on the grid

definitions.text: Fraction of New York lights found here — on the grid

parts.words: Fraction of New York lights found here — on the grid
parts.note: a part of Manhattan, and also the right-hand part of a crossword grid, where many lights (answers) sit

explanation.walkthrough: Read one way it is the Manhattan district glittering at night; read as a crossword, lights are answers and this region of the grid is where many of them are entered.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Side is a district of Manhattan; on a map-oriented grid, east is the right-hand side.

clue.text: Loss of cohesion is disastrously disorientating

indicators.note: disastrously suggests things going badly wrong, so the letters of disorientating are rearranged

explanation.surface: Falling apart is a terribly bewildering experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Disintegration is the process of breaking up into fragments, losing unity.

clue.text: Fashionable people in command producing tension

parts.note: the ton is an old word for high society, the fashionable set
IC is the abbreviation for in charge or in command

explanation.surface: Trendy people in charge are creating stress.
explanation.definitionFit: In physiology, tonic describes sustained muscular contraction, a state of tension or tone.

clue.text: Slim fit of pants not to be discussed

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or bad, so these words are poorly arranged and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tight pair of trousers is a taboo subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slim fit of pants' reads as a style of trousers; pants here is the British slang adjective meaning rubbish, signalling the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject that is off-limits is forbidden territory, not open for conversation.

clue.text: Classy schemes about foremost of designated high-lying areas

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in the old U and non-U distinction

indicators.note: about means the schemes go round the next letter

parts.note: schemes are plans

indicators.note: foremost of picks the opening letter of designated

explanation.surface: Upmarket development plans concern certain designated hillside regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Uplands are elevated stretches of country, hills and plateaux above the lowlands.

clue.text: Muscle's instant power succeeded

parts.note: a trice is an instant, as in 'in a trice'
P is the physics abbreviation for power
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A muscle's sudden strength won the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the large muscle at the back of the upper arm that straightens the elbow.

clue.text: The gradients exceptionally relieved of bends

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the ordinary, so the words The gradients are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hills on a road have been unusually smoothed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A road that is straightened has had its curves removed, so it runs in a line.

clue.text: Secondary school for little James, it's said, for starters not a success, introduced with hesitation

indicators.note: it's said means the name is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: Jim is a short form of James

indicators.note: for starters picks the opening letters of not, a, success and introduced

parts.note: um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Young Jim, apparently a flop at his school, is admitted after some dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gymnasium is the academic secondary school in Germany and some other European countries.

clue.text: Worn out foolish endeavours northern America abandons

indicators.note: foolish suggests the letters are scrambled senselessly into a new order
abandons means the letters for northern and America are left out of the mix

explanation.surface: Silly attempts are tiresome once America walks away from the North.
explanation.definitionFit: Overused means employed so often that it has become hackneyed or stale.

clue.text: Peculiar borders of territory in land one owns

parts.note: proper can mean peculiar, belonging specifically to something, as in 'proper to'

indicators.note: borders of picks the outside letters of territory, its first and last

explanation.surface: Strange edges of a region within a landowner's estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Property is real estate, the land and buildings that belong to someone.

clue.text: Type of reflection of worth involving famous boxer pursued by periodical

indicators.note: involving means the word for worth takes in the next pieces

parts.note: virtue is worth or merit

indicators.note: pursued by means the boxer comes first with the periodical following him

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the famous heavyweight
a mag is a magazine, a periodical

explanation.surface: A reflective piece on merit about a great boxer, followed up in a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtual image is one formed where light rays only appear to meet, as in a mirror reflection.

clue.text: Form bookmaker used upset old tax company

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the pieces are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A betting shop's outdated tax firm has been toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' suggests a turf accountant, but here it is a maker of books: a printer or binder.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavo is a book size made by folding a printed sheet into eight leaves.

clue.text: Accept, we're told, 50 in emolument for subsidiary action

indicators.note: we're told means the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to buy an idea is to accept it

indicators.note: in means the numeral sits inside the word for emolument

parts.note: emolument means pay or salary
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Agree, apparently, to fifty within your salary.
explanation.definitionFit: By-play is secondary action going on alongside the main action, especially on stage.

clue.text: Highly esteemed place surrounded by grass

indicators.note: surrounded by means the word for place sits within the word for grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
to place is to put

explanation.surface: A well-regarded spot hemmed in by lawns.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed can mean held in good repute, enjoying a high reputation.

clue.text: Shelley's dismal daughter back

parts.note: rear means back

explanation.surface: The poet Shelley's gloomy girl returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic word for dreary, used by Romantic poets such as Shelley.

clue.text: Article shrewdly rejecting Liberal chaos

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: rejecting means the Liberal letter is thrown out of the word for shrewdly

parts.note: archly means slyly or knowingly, in a shrewd way

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece cleverly dismissing the Liberal party's disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is a state of lawless disorder, with no authority in control.

clue.text: African plain's surprisingly greenest before onset of inundations

indicators.note: before places the rearranged letters ahead of the next piece
surprisingly hints the letters of greenest turn up in an unexpected order
onset of picks the opening letter of inundations

explanation.surface: The savannah is lusher than ever ahead of the floods.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast savannah grassland in Tanzania, famous for its wildlife migrations.

clue.text: Altogether ultimately out of bounds

indicators.note: out of bounds means the word for ultimately loses its boundary letters at each end

parts.note: ultimately means finally, in the end

explanation.surface: Taken as a whole, the area ends up forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of bounds' looks like part of the definition, but it tells you to strip the first and last letters, F and Y, from FINALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: In all means in total, counting everything together.

clue.text: On the radio confuse periods of time

indicators.note: on the radio means the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to daze is to confuse or stun

explanation.surface: Broadcasts muddle up the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: Days are units of time, each lasting twenty-four hours.

clue.text: Point of concert being performed by Conservative

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, like the BBC Proms
a show that is on is being performed
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: The main feature of a concert staged by a Tory politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A promontory is a headland, a point of high land jutting out into the sea.
